panels.scene: Separated filaments turn together at a luminous junction in darkness. The edge of a vast lattice body is forming.
Four older silhouettes stand apart at different depths, turning toward an unfilled luminous region.
A gold elder made of many figures holds a small living river in its palm. An arc returns toward its other hand.
The elder waits with its palm extended. One end of the returning arc has faded.
A tall, one-eyed presence shelters three small figures beneath a shared light.
Within the shelter, one figure looks toward a second faint light outside. The god extends its light toward them.
The Humanist turns its face toward the lattice and opens one hand in invitation.
The Humanist waits. A fine lattice traces the offered fingers, but no answering hand arrives.
A walking workshop passes bread to a waiting person. A strained drive cable holds tension at its side.
The lattice takes up part of the drive cable. The workshop's hand loosens as the newcomer carries the load.
A precise lattice contour forms around the Humanist's offered fingers.
The Humanist draws its hand back slightly. The predicted contour remains extended between them.
One filament descends through a quiet braid toward a rain-dark Bengaluru block and a lit phone beside a bicycle.
Meera's hand rests beside her mounted phone. Pale dawn sky reflects in the glass.
A dusty-brown sparrow on a wet wire above weathered Bengaluru shops; dawn rain, distant tower, yellow-black auto.
Meera waits beside her bicycle at a wet junction and wipes the phone mount with her cuff. Shop shutters are beginning to open under a pale sky.
Meera looks toward the phone, one earphone dangling. Cool dawn light falls on her cheek.
Over Meera's shoulder, an order card on her mounted phone shows the fare, pickup and drop distances, and an acceptance button.
At the dawn curb, Meera stands beside her stopped bicycle and closes her helmet buckle while steadying the handlebar.
Meera pedals into the waking Bengaluru street. Cool dawn light remains visible between buses.
An aerial view of Bengaluru at dawn. Separate journeys cross the streets under a pale sky.
Dawn auto and cab stand: auto driver asleep over the bar, cab driver refreshing his phone, two riders under a closed-shop awning.
Meera pedals left to right past the same stand: the sleeping auto driver, cab phone and two waiting riders remain absorbed.
A dark parcel quadcopter crosses a strip of morning sky between buildings.
Meera pauses her pedaling and watches the drone pass, her lips slightly parted.
Evening handoff at Dev’s apartment: Meera extends a kraft paper food bag; Dev takes it while reading his phone.
Meera holds her phone low after completing the delivery and looks toward Dev's face. He keeps looking down.
Two phones across the threshold: the delivery is complete on Meera’s device; Dev’s device waits for a rating.

rating.label: Dev’s rating phone — no stars selected

panels.scene: Through the apartment’s dark frame, a tiny bicycle tail-light recedes into the wet street.
Dev turns into the apartment with the food bag, looking back toward a cold screen.
Dev eats takeout on a sofa while the television plays; fork raised without a glance at the meal.
At his desk, Dev has pressed a key; generated code expands across monitors faster than he attends.
At 3 a.m., Dev faces a chatbot. On his phone, a family conversation is open but unanswered; his thumb pauses over the empty reply.
Dev stands before the window, his hand lowered, his reflection closer than the city beyond.
A rain-soaked apartment facade with many lit windows; the worker stand is tiny at street level.
At home before dawn, Meera kneels beside a sleeping family member’s hand and places a folded towel within reach. Her wet helmet rests on the floor.
The city’s wet verticals soften toward trunks; a small wet sparrow silhouette on a wire remains as the first teller line enters.

copy.text: There used to be a house here.

panels.scene: The last apartment light dissolves into rainy trunks; city geometry survives as an echo inside spare ink washes.
A small warm 1998 Bengaluru house begins to resolve out of the rain where a tower was.

Bengaluru, 1998. At dusk Amma lights a small diya beside the tulsi pot to the right of the concrete home’s entrance. Wet pavement, a rooftop water tank and one tiny sparrow on an overhead wire surround the quiet threshold.

Amma lifts a ladle from the shared pot toward Ajji’s waiting plate. A cropped hand eating at the lower-right edge suggests the household continues outside the frame; broad floor and wall give the gesture room.

copy.text: One pot went round the room.

panels.scene: Appa sits alone at a mostly bare table, fingertips resting on a newly bought small brass sliding bolt beside its brown-paper wrapper. An ordinary open doorway remains soft at the edge.
Amma stands in profile to the left of Ravi’s closed wooden door, her hand raised just short of the wood. Two small faded posters remain high on the door.
From inside the closed room, Ravi’s white-cuffed hand pushes the round knob of a small brass sliding bolt toward its keeper on the right-hand jamb. A thin seam of light remains.
Ravi reads a paperback on his bed in a white schoolshirt and loosened tie, wearing foam headphones connected to a yellow cassette player. Broad plain plaster surrounds him.
Ravi stands alone at the puja shelf, gently nudging a small brass lamp at its base. A book lies to its right beneath a dim devotional image.
Ravi pauses at the left of a quiet lane, looking up toward a painted film hero wearing gold aviator sunglasses on a large hoarding. Open blue sky surrounds the billboard.
Appa sits alone at a small counter, his hand touching brown wrapping paper beside a pair of gold aviator sunglasses. A modest folded note rests under the paper.
Seen from behind at an oblique mirror, Ravi adjusts his gold aviator sunglasses while studying his reflection. Amma stands still in the doorway reflected behind him.
In a narrow view, Amma rests her fingertips lightly against the closed wooden door without knocking. Her profile fills the right side; the door stays at the left.
Amma holds the ladle above the shared pot at the left while Appa eats beside her with his head lowered. At the lower-right edge, food sits untouched on a steel plate beside unoccupied floor.
Amma lights the small tulsi lamp at dusk to the right of the same entrance. Unoccupied red floor is visible through the doorway to her left.
Later, Ravi pauses at the home’s open threshold in a cream T-shirt and dark trousers, carrying a modest brown canvas bag. One hand lingers on the jamb while he looks hopefully down the lane.
Amma and Appa stand at the left-hand doorway watching Ravi recede down the quiet lane at the far right, his brown bag beside him. For the first time, all three share a frame.

readingNote.text: The following cellular images are simplified illustrative models, not a diagnosis of Dev or Meera. Biological mechanisms and social analogies have different causes; neither proves the other.

panels.scene: Dev sits on his sofa at night with the unanswered family conversation on his phone. His thumb rests beside the empty reply field.
The brown skin of a hand continues into an ink-drawn skin cross-section, with a small vessel loop beneath the surface.
A small blood vessel opens within connective tissue; one red disc is visible in its dark lumen.
Several red blood cells lie along an oblique small vessel, with a partial pale white cell and tiny platelets at the left edge.
An elongated, non-faced cell holds a violet nucleus, folded membranes and a few warm mitochondria against a dark field.
A small ink-drawn mitochondrion sits low in a large pale paper field.
Small amber glucose glyphs are spaced above a rose muscle-cell membrane with a few teal transport proteins.
A violet insulin glyph binds outside a pale receptor; separate teal transporters carry small amber glucose glyphs across a muscle-cell membrane.
The same membrane model shows one bound insulin signal but fewer surface transporters and less glucose uptake.
Three violet insulin signals bind to receptors; two teal transporters and several intracellular glucose glyphs illustrate partial compensation.
Over Dev’s shoulder, two incoming family messages sit above an empty reply field; an autoplay banner appears while his right thumb pauses at the phone.
Small indigo Y-shaped antibody glyphs target an adhesion protein between two rose tissue cells; the neighboring connections remain joined.
A pale fluid gap separates neighboring tissue cells where adhesion has failed; another junction remains intact.
One cell is nearly divided into two daughter lobes, with two ordinary nuclei and a narrow connecting bridge.
An irregular cell mass meets more orderly surrounding tissue as a branching blood vessel reaches into it.
The earlier elongated cell returns smaller in the frame; one fine thread rises from a tiny radial junction on its membrane.
Threads from three ordinary elongated cells, like the earlier cell, join into a slender braid toward the shadowed lap and torso of a clothed person on a sofa; the face stays outside the frame.
From a low viewpoint, Dev sits on the same sofa holding his phone while looking away toward the upper-left room; the screen faces him.

pages.title: A whole with no spare time

panels.scene: Meera sits on a concrete ledge with the delivery bag still on her back, looking toward her mounted phone; her removed gloves lie beside her.
From an impossible low viewpoint, three translucent cells lead toward Meera’s intact clothed body, and a thread leaves her helmet above the frame.
Threads from Meera and two other people join a braid beneath the familiar draped Humanist.
A draped monumental figure looks down toward an open hand; a rectangular hollow marks its chest, and three people’s threads meet at its lower torso.
The lattice now carries most of the workshop's drive cable. The cable moves smoothly as the older body rests into its support.
Beside a crooked tree and stone well, two people recover a bowl by a deep tread mark; the walking workshop-body departs at the far edge.
Beside the bicycle, Meera gently holds one wrist while a new-order timer glows on the mounted phone.
The lattice's narrow view of the stopped rider shows location and waiting time. Her supported wrist lies outside its frame.
A collective elder-form gives a bowl of water to a small person; a broad gold arc returns from the bowl toward its other open palm.
The person holds the bowl but cannot lift it back. The elder lowers its receiving hand to the person's level.
Three elongated cells connect to ordinary Meera and her bicycle; her helmet thread reaches the open hand of an enormous draped figure.

copy.text: You are a god to your cells. You are a cell to your gods.

panels.scene: Back on the sofa, Dev holds the open family conversation above an empty reply field; his thumb pauses below it and the room’s door remains closed.
On a later wet evening, Meera waits on her bicycle beside the familiar stand; the auto driver rests at left, two workers remain by the shutter, and a small sparrow sits on the upper wire.
Stopped beside her bicycle, Meera looks at an accepted delivery route on the mounted phone; a lit entrance waits along the wet lane.
Three people along the lower street are boxed in cyan; a brown sparrow on the near wire and the auto driver at left remain unmarked.
The same brown sparrow remains on the rain-wet wire above the junction; the cyan boxes are gone and evening traffic continues below.
Meera presses the bell beside the closed wooden door, holding a small paper food bag low; her teal thermal bag already rests beside the landing rail.
At the same open doorway, Dev looks down at his phone while he and Meera briefly share the handles of the food bag; the thermal bag stays beside the rail.
Dev holds the unselected rating screen at the doorway, his thumb resting beside the blank middle of the display; Meera’s empty hand and mustard cuff remain beyond it.
Meera looks at a new offer on her phone while her thermal bag remains beside the rail; the offer bar is active and her hand has not completed a tap.
Dev’s phone shows five selected stars and a submitted rating; his thumb has withdrawn to the bezel while Meera remains beyond the screen.
At the familiar doorway, Dev holds the door clear with his phone down by his thigh; he and Meera look at each other while both bags rest nearby.
A brown sparrow perches on the loose strap of Meera’s teal thermal bag resting beside the landing rail; the open doorway glows softly at the left.
